fixes.explanation: Moses, Israel's leader, says it right out: “Destroy completely all the places where the nations you are dispossessing have served their gods…” (Deuteronomy 12:2). Completely, friend. That's not scraping the black off one burnt cookie, that's the whole tray going in the trash. I'd say that word was picked on purpose.

Nice guess, but Moses never hands the choice to the priests. He says Israel must seek “…the place the LORD your God will choose…” (Deuteronomy 12:5). The LORD picks the spot. That's like being told exactly where the party is and your only job is to show up with the cookies.

Moses doesn't mention an army camp. He says the LORD will establish the place “…as a dwelling for His Name…” (Deuteronomy 12:5). Dwelling is the word he uses, friend, and I'll stick with it. I think a dwelling sounds a lot more like a home than a barracks.

No school of prophets shows up in this verse. Moses says the LORD will establish the place “…as a dwelling for His Name…” (Deuteronomy 12:5). That's a home address, friend, not a program list. I think the LORD picked a warm word there.

Moses says, “You are not to do as we are doing here today, where everyone does what seems right in his own eyes.” (Deuteronomy 12:8). Notice he says “we.” A boss who says “we really need to be on time” is usually pointing at you. Moses is counting himself in.

An altar isn't the reason Moses gives. He says, “For you have not yet come to the resting place and the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.” (Deuteronomy 12:9). That's like asking for a finished batch while the dough is still in the bowl. The arrival is still ahead, and the word yet is doing the heavy lifting.

Moses lists who rejoices before the LORD and includes “…the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.” (Deuteronomy 12:12). He comes right after the menservants and maidservants. The Levite has a seat in the rejoicing, friend. Pull up a chair.

Right gates, wrong guest. Moses reads the list and the name at the end is “…the Levite within your gates…” (Deuteronomy 12:12). Swapping in the foreigner is like putting the wrong name on a cookie box. The Levite is the one Moses names.

True. Moses is listing who rejoices before the LORD, and he names the Levite, adding “…since he has no portion or inheritance among you.” (Deuteronomy 12:12). That's the detail he attaches to the Levite. I think it's a kind one, friend.

Moses says, “Both the ceremonially clean and unclean may eat it as they would a gazelle or deer…” (Deuteronomy 12:15). So this everyday meat is allowed for both. Same meat, same permission, friend. The clean and the unclean can both enjoy it.

Moses says, “…but you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.” (Deuteronomy 12:16). That's the firm limit he names on this meat. He gives the reason later: “…the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.” (Deuteronomy 12:23). Blood gets poured out, friend.

Skin doesn't come up in this verse. Moses says, “…but you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.” (Deuteronomy 12:16). Blood is the one thing he names. I love a clear instruction, friend, because I've followed recipes that just said bake until done and left me guessing.

The edge of their own fields isn't what this verse names. Moses says, “…you must eat them in the presence of the LORD your God at the place the LORD your God will choose…” (Deuteronomy 12:18). He points them to the chosen place. That's like planning the big family gathering and then everybody eating in their own cars.

Moses says, “…be careful not to neglect the Levites as long as you live in your land.” (Deuteronomy 12:19). Just before this, he names the Levite among those eating at the chosen place. I think Moses wants the Levites remembered. And notice the words as long as you live in your land.

Follow sounds reasonable, but it's not Moses' word. He says, “…be careful not to neglect the Levites as long as you live in your land.” (Deuteronomy 12:19). Swapping in follow turns a warning into a parade. Neglect is the word to keep, friend.

Moses says, “The blood of your other sacrifices must be poured out beside the altar of the LORD your God, but you may eat the meat.” (Deuteronomy 12:27). Burnt offerings go on the altar, meat and blood. For the other sacrifices, the blood is poured out and the meat is permitted to be eaten. That's the permission Moses gives, friend.

That's how Moses describes the burnt offerings: “…the meat and blood of your burnt offerings on the altar…” (Deuteronomy 12:27). For the other sacrifices, he says “…but you may eat the meat.” So the permission he gives there is to eat. Two kinds of offering, friend, two different instructions.

Moses warns against asking about their gods, and he puts these words in Israel's mouth: “How do these nations serve their gods? I will do likewise.” (Deuteronomy 12:30). The trap is the asking, and then the copying. It starts as curiosity and ends as imitation, friend.
